events.title: British Forces Evacuate Boston
events.description: After George Washington and Henry Knox placed artillery on the heights overlooking the city, British troops and Loyalists sailed out of Boston. It was the end of an eleven-month siege.
events.significance: The evacuation was the first major American victory of the Revolutionary War. It is still celebrated in Massachusetts as Evacuation Day.

events.title: National Gallery of Art Opens in Washington
events.description: President Franklin D. Roosevelt officially opened the National Gallery of Art on the National Mall in Washington, DC.
events.significance: The gallery became one of the world's great art museums and gave the public free access to a major national art collection.

events.title: Golda Meir Becomes Israel's Prime Minister
events.description: Golda Meir took office as prime minister of Israel. She was the country's first woman to hold the post.
events.significance: Meir was among the first women in modern times to lead a national government. She led Israel through the 1973 Yom Kippur War.

events.title: South African Whites Vote to End Apartheid
events.description: In a referendum, 68.7 percent of white South African voters backed negotiating an end to apartheid and racial segregation.
events.significance: The vote gave President F. W. de Klerk a mandate to negotiate with the African National Congress. That cleared the way for the 1994 democratic elections.
